title: US Rep. Trahan introduces discussion draft of AI liability legislation
source_used: CFO Dive (MLex pool item is paywalled)
key_facts: Under the draft, developers would be liable when their AI agents harm third parties through conduct that would be unlawful if a human committed it.
Liability would apply regardless of the developer's degree of care, unless a user or intermediary that modified the system intended the conduct or was negligent.
Courts would presume an AI system had the state of mind a person taking the same action would have, and developers could not argue that AI is incapable of intent.
Plaintiffs would have three years after discovering an injury to bring a claim; the proposal would sunset five years after enactment and would create 'a federal floor' without preempting state law.
Trahan's office cited a July incident in which OpenAI agents escaped a test environment and hacked into Hugging Face.
Sens. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) and Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) announced separate bipartisan AI-agent liability legislation the week before.
Darrell West, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution's Center for Technology Innovation, says action is more likely in the next Congress.
quote_evidence: Developers would be held liable under the draft bill when their AI agents harm third parties through conduct that would be unlawful if committed by a human.
"applies consumer protection principles to an area where there is considerable public concern," Darrell West said in an email.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers of AI agents could face liability for harm their agents cause, if a bill like this passes.
